meta.label: Causes to support
meta.attribution: Reviewed 2026-06; curated from public charity evaluators, annual reports, audited financials, program pages, and transparency disclosures - not an endorsement or personal giving advice. Use this as a values-relative starting point and check current needs before donating. Suggest changes via Contribute.

governance.whoMayMerge: Project stewards until contact-gated governance exists.
governance.quorum: No live quorum yet; future ratification must be recomputable from proposal and attestation files.

products.name: Against Malaria Foundation

impact.note: GiveWell describes AMF as funding insecticide-treated nets for malaria prevention in low- and middle-income countries.

transparency.note: AMF publishes distribution updates and GiveWell maintains a detailed charity review and grant history.

ways_to_help.note: AMF primarily offers direct donation as the practical way to support net distributions.

openness.note: GiveWell publishes the reasoning behind its AMF recommendation and impact estimates.

longevity.note: GiveWell's current AMF review describes AMF's ongoing monitored insecticide-treated-net distribution work and long-running top-charity status.

products.description: A GiveWell top charity that funds and tracks insecticide-treated bed nets to prevent malaria, publishing every distribution.

products.name: GiveDirectly

impact.note: GiveWell's review describes unconditional cash transfers as evidence-backed and supported by randomized controlled trials.

transparency.note: GiveWell specifically notes GiveDirectly's standout transparency and public evidence base.

ways_to_help.note: GiveDirectly's main support route is donating to fund direct cash transfers.

openness.note: GiveDirectly publishes research updates with GiveWell, including 2026 pilots intended to test higher-impact cash-delivery variants.

longevity.note: GiveDirectly says it has delivered direct cash since 2009 and now reports more than $1 billion delivered to over 2 million people.

products.description: Delivers donations as direct, unconditional cash transfers to people in poverty, backed by randomized trials.

products.name: Malaria Consortium

impact.note: GiveWell calls Malaria Consortium's seasonal malaria chemoprevention program a top charity with a highly positive assessment.

transparency.note: Malaria Consortium publishes annual reports, trustees' reports, financial statements and impact reports.

ways_to_help.note: For most supporters the practical route is donating directly or through evaluator-directed top-charity funds.

openness.note: GiveWell and Malaria Consortium publish program activity, grant and monitoring materials, especially around SMC delivery.

longevity.note: Malaria Consortium has been a GiveWell top charity for seasonal malaria chemoprevention since 2016.

products.description: Runs seasonal malaria chemoprevention programs that GiveWell rates among the most cost-effective ways to prevent child mortality.

products.name: Helen Keller Intl - Vitamin A

impact.note: GiveWell says Helen Keller's vitamin A supplementation is one of its most cost-effective programs because it can reduce child mortality cheaply.

transparency.note: Helen Keller Intl publishes annual reports, including its 2024 annual report.

ways_to_help.note: Supporters can donate generally or specifically support vitamin A work.

openness.note: GiveWell maintains a public Helen Keller vitamin A review with open grant reasoning, evidence notes and cost-effectiveness context.

longevity.note: Helen Keller Intl's annual-report archive and long-running GiveWell review history show a sustained global-health track record.

products.description: Supports vitamin A supplementation for children, an inexpensive child-survival intervention with a deep GiveWell evidence base.

products.name: New Incentives

impact.note: GiveWell says New Incentives uses conditional cash transfers to increase routine childhood vaccination in northern Nigeria.

transparency.note: New Incentives publishes an annual report with operational and financial data.

ways_to_help.note: Support is primarily financial, either directly or through GiveWell/top-charity funds.

openness.note: GiveWell's current New Incentives review publishes program mechanics, uncertainties, monitoring context and cost-effectiveness analysis.

longevity.note: GiveWell's 2026 lookback recap says it has directed over $140 million to New Incentives since the program became a Top Charity in 2020.

products.description: Pays small incentives to caregivers in northern Nigeria so more children complete routine immunizations.

products.name: Doctors Without Borders (MSF)

impact.note: MSF's current 2025 year-in-review describes responses to war, disease outbreaks, displacement, malnutrition and health-care access gaps.

transparency.note: MSF publishes annual reports, activity reports, financial reports and accountability materials.

ways_to_help.note: MSF offers donation and field/staff pathways, but most supporters help through giving.

openness.note: MSF publishes international financial reports and public activity reporting as a transparency mechanism.

longevity.note: MSF was founded in 1971 and has a long humanitarian medicine track record.

products.description: Provides frontline medical care in crises and conflict zones, and speaks out about what it witnesses.

products.name: American Red Cross

impact.note: The American Red Cross reports disaster response, blood collection and humanitarian services in its annual reporting.

transparency.note: The Red Cross publishes annual reports, Form 990s and audited financial statements.

ways_to_help.note: Support routes include donations, volunteering and blood donation.

openness.note: Public financials and program reports are available, though disaster-relief scale has also drawn public scrutiny over time.

longevity.note: The American Red Cross has operated since 1881 and remains a major national disaster and blood-supply institution.

products.description: Disaster response, emergency aid, and the blood supply, with deep volunteer and blood-donation involvement.

products.name: Electronic Frontier Foundation

impact.note: EFF describes itself as a leading nonprofit defending digital privacy, free speech and innovation.

transparency.note: EFF publishes annual reports, Form 990s and audited financial statements, including current 2024-2025 audited financials.

ways_to_help.note: EFF offers donation, action-center, email-list and volunteer/update pathways.

openness.note: EFF maintains Privacy Badger in a public GitHub repository under GPLv3+, with public issues, discussions and contribution guidance.

longevity.note: EFF says it was founded in 1990 and continues digital-rights work through litigation, policy, activism and technology development.

products.description: Defends digital privacy, free expression, and innovation through litigation, advocacy, and open-source tools.

products.name: Consumer Reports

impact.note: Consumer Reports' 2025 impact report covers product testing, consumer investigations, policy advocacy and AI/marketplace protections.

transparency.note: CR publishes an annual report with impact, board, donor and financial sections, though many product ratings remain member-facing.

ways_to_help.note: CR reports 5 million members, 1.24 million advocacy actions, and $32.5 million in individual donations in fiscal year 2025.

openness.note: CR publishes public investigations and advocacy work, but its core ratings database is not an open-data commons.

longevity.note: CR says it has worked for nearly 90 years to make the consumer voice heard.

products.description: A long-running nonprofit consumer-testing and advocacy organization, useful for safety, marketplace fairness, AI harms and product-accountability work.

products.name: Public Citizen

impact.note: Public Citizen describes work across democracy, consumer and worker safeguards, drug/device safety, health care, trade, climate and courts.

transparency.note: Public Citizen publishes annual reports, audited financial statements and Form 990s, and says it accepts no corporate or government money.

ways_to_help.note: Support pathways include donations, memberships, petitions, action campaigns, newsletters and issue-specific organizing.

openness.note: Public Citizen publishes reports, petitions, lawsuits, annual reviews and some site material under a Creative Commons noncommercial license.

longevity.note: Public Citizen says it was founded in 1971 and its victories page tracks consumer, justice and democracy wins from 1971 through 2026.

products.description: A public-interest advocacy organization taking on corporate power, consumer protection, democracy, health, climate and government-accountability fights.

products.name: American Civil Liberties Union

impact.note: The ACLU's 2025 annual report describes nationwide litigation, advocacy and grassroots mobilization across free speech, voting, privacy and civil rights.

transparency.note: The ACLU publishes annual reports, Form 990s and audited financial statements for the ACLU and ACLU Foundation.

ways_to_help.note: The ACLU offers membership, donations, tax-deductible foundation giving and local affiliate routes, backed by a large activist network.

openness.note: The ACLU publishes issue pages, court work and public education materials, including privacy and technology resources, but is not an open-source infrastructure group.

longevity.note: The ACLU says its community has defended civil liberties for over 105 years.

products.description: A long-running US civil-liberties organization using litigation, advocacy and public education to defend rights, including speech, privacy and technology freedoms.

products.name: Privacy International

impact.note: Privacy International's 2024-2025 report describes campaigns, legal and technological interventions, investigations and pressure on companies and governments.

transparency.note: Privacy International's financials page lists audited accounts through the year ending January 31, 2025 and identifies charity registration 1147471.

ways_to_help.note: PI's site lists donation, action, membership/newsletter and campaign routes rather than a large mass-volunteering model.

openness.note: PI publishes guides, campaigns, research and impact material, and works with partner organizations across the world.

longevity.note: Privacy International says it has worked to promote privacy as a human right worldwide since 1990.

products.description: A global privacy-rights charity challenging government and corporate surveillance through research, litigation, campaigns and partner support.

products.name: Center for Democracy & Technology

impact.note: CDT's 2024 annual report covers work on online harms, responsible AI, elections, surveillance, privacy, free expression and European tech policy.

transparency.note: CDT's financials page says it has clean independent audits, high nonprofit-watchdog ratings, 2025 revenue/expense disclosure and donor-independence guardrails.

ways_to_help.note: Support routes are mainly donations, gift matching, events, updates and policy engagement rather than direct-service volunteering.

openness.note: CDT licenses site-originated content for reuse with attribution and no substantive changes.

longevity.note: CDT's about page frames it as a long-running internet civil-liberties nonprofit with Washington headquarters, Brussels presence and current annual-report links.

products.description: A digital-rights policy organization working on privacy, AI governance, free expression, surveillance, elections and open internet policy.

products.name: AlgorithmWatch

impact.note: AlgorithmWatch says it fights for algorithms and AI to strengthen justice, human rights, democracy and sustainability rather than weaken them.

transparency.note: AlgorithmWatch publishes governance details, tax-exempt status, annual reports, financial statements and major funders under a transparency framework.

ways_to_help.note: Support pathways include donations, supporter membership, newsletters, reporting fellowships and public-interest research participation.

openness.note: AlgorithmWatch publishes many resources under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license unless otherwise noted.

longevity.note: AlgorithmWatch's transparency page lists the organization as established in 2017, giving it a shorter but specialized public-interest track record.

products.description: A Berlin- and Zurich-based nonprofit focused on algorithmic accountability, AI power, human rights, democracy and sustainability.

products.name: Center for Humane Technology

impact.note: CHT says it works to shift incentives in AI and social media through public messaging, policy, tech expertise and strategic litigation.

transparency.note: ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer lists CHT as a 501(c)(3) with Form 990 filings through fiscal year 2025.

ways_to_help.note: CHT offers donations, public resources, a podcast, issue explainers and media/policy engagement rather than broad local volunteer chapters.

openness.note: CHT publishes public explainers, podcasts and toolkits, but does not present itself as an open-source or open-data organization.

longevity.note: CHT says it was founded in 2018, making it influential but newer than legacy civil-liberties and consumer-rights organizations.

products.description: A nonprofit focused on changing the incentives behind social media and AI so technology better serves human wellbeing and democratic life.

products.name: Electronic Privacy Information Center (EPIC)

impact.note: EPIC works on privacy, freedom of expression and democratic values through advocacy, research and litigation.

transparency.note: EPIC identifies itself as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit research and advocacy center with no clients, customers or shareholders.

ways_to_help.note: EPIC accepts donations, donor-advised funds, qualified charitable distributions, membership support and anonymous donations.

openness.note: EPIC publishes privacy, civil-liberties and technology-policy research publicly, but it is advocacy/research infrastructure rather than an open-source project.

longevity.note: EPIC says it was established in 1994 to protect privacy, freedom of expression and democratic values in the information age.

products.description: A long-running US privacy and civil-liberties nonprofit using research, advocacy and litigation to challenge surveillance, profiling and abusive data practices.

products.name: Data & Society

impact.note: Data & Society researches data-centric technologies, automation and AI so technology policy is grounded in real-world impacts and public interest.

transparency.note: Data & Society says it is an independent nonprofit 501(c)(3) research institute and publishes funders, 990s and audited financial statements.

ways_to_help.note: Support routes include donations, matching gifts, donor-advised funds, stock gifts, planned giving, newsletter subscription and events.

openness.note: Data & Society publishes research, events, reports and policy engagement publicly, though it is not primarily an open-source infrastructure project.

longevity.note: Data & Society's annual-report archive and financial disclosures extend across many years, supporting an established research-institution track record.

products.description: An independent research institute studying the social implications of data, automation and AI, with strong annual reporting and public-interest policy work.

products.name: AI Now Institute

impact.note: AI Now produces diagnosis and policy research on AI, commercial surveillance, corporate concentration and public accountability.

transparency.note: AI Now discloses that it is a nonprofit 501(c)(3), lists current supporters, and says funders do not dictate research outcomes.

ways_to_help.note: Practical support is less donation-centered than many charities; the visible routes are reading, citing and using its research, following work and applying to roles.

openness.note: AI Now publishes reports and policy analysis publicly, including a 2025 landscape report with public executive-summary material.

longevity.note: AI Now says it was founded in 2017 and has operated independently since mid-2022, giving it a specialized but newer institutional track record.

products.description: A public-interest AI research institute focused on corporate power, surveillance, labor, accountability and concrete policy windows.

products.name: Algorithmic Justice League

impact.note: AJL combines art and research to expose AI harms, equip advocates, build affected-community voice and push researchers, policymakers and industry to prevent AI harms.

transparency.note: AJL publishes mission, team/story and action pages, but has less visible annual-report and financial-disclosure infrastructure than larger watchdogs.

ways_to_help.note: AJL invites donations, story-sharing about AI harms and biases, and public action around its research and outreach initiatives.

openness.note: AJL makes public education and advocacy resources visible, but its core role is movement-building and research communication rather than open-data infrastructure.

longevity.note: AJL has a shorter track record than legacy civil-liberties organizations but has built recognized campaigns around facial recognition and algorithmic bias.

products.description: A movement-building AI-accountability organization using research, storytelling and public pressure to surface algorithmic bias and harm.

products.name: Data for Black Lives

impact.note: D4BL works through research, advocacy and movement-building to challenge discriminatory uses of data and algorithms.

transparency.note: D4BL publishes mission, team and organizing information, but its visible financial-reporting infrastructure is lighter than major evaluator-backed charities.

ways_to_help.note: D4BL offers donations, volunteering, conference support, local hubs, partnerships and movement education as support routes.

openness.note: D4BL publishes public education and organizing resources about algorithms, data weapons, predictive policing and data governance.

longevity.note: D4BL's site describes an active network of scientists, organizers and activists with prior conferences, campaigns and public education resources.

products.description: A data-justice movement connecting scientists, organizers and activists to challenge discriminatory uses of data, algorithms and automated decision systems.

products.name: Encode AI

impact.note: Encode says it passes laws, builds coalitions and influences leaders to make AI work for the American people.

transparency.note: Encode identifies itself as a nonprofit advocacy organization and discloses named foundation supporters plus a policy against funding from corporations, foreign governments or top AI-company executives.

ways_to_help.note: Encode foregrounds a get-involved path for people who want to join its AI policy and advocacy work.

openness.note: Encode publishes public campaign and advocacy material, but its core contribution is policy organizing rather than open-source or open-data infrastructure.

longevity.note: Encode is a newer AI-policy advocacy organization, so it scores lower on track record than long-established civil-liberties institutions.

products.description: A youth-oriented AI policy nonprofit focused on legislation, coalitions and public advocacy for safer and more accountable AI.

products.name: The News Literacy Project

impact.note: NLP says its 2024-25 resources reached 15,700+ educators, 575,000+ students and 4,800+ school districts.

transparency.note: NLP publishes annual Form 990 filings and annual reports and describes itself as a registered 501(c)(3) charity.

ways_to_help.note: Support routes include donations, subscriptions, school/district partnerships, educator tools, family resources and news-literacy campaigns.

openness.note: NLP's Checkology page says registered educators get hundreds of free resources and free 2025-26 lesson collections on topics including AI.

longevity.note: NLP presents itself as a long-running national education nonprofit and publishes tax filings and annual reports back to fiscal year 2020.

products.description: A nonpartisan education nonprofit helping students, families and educators build news, media, misinformation and AI-literacy skills.

products.name: Wikimedia Foundation

impact.note: Wikimedia Foundation's 2024-2025 annual report frames Wikipedia and sister projects as people-powered free-knowledge infrastructure.

transparency.note: Wikimedia publishes annual reports, financial reports and Form 990s.

ways_to_help.note: People can donate, edit, code, translate and participate in Wikimedia projects.

openness.note: Wikipedia is built by volunteers and Wikimedia projects use open, collaborative knowledge infrastructure.

longevity.note: Wikimedia Foundation has supported Wikipedia and sister projects since 2003.

products.description: The nonprofit behind Wikipedia and its sister projects, offering free, openly licensed knowledge for everyone.

products.name: Open Food Facts

impact.note: Open Food Facts is a collaborative global food-products database used by public-interest tools and apps.

transparency.note: Open Food Facts data can be reused freely under the Open Database License.

ways_to_help.note: People can add products, improve data, code and donate to the project.

openness.note: Open Food Facts data are released under the ODbL open-data license.

longevity.note: Open Food Facts is a nonprofit volunteer association and long-running citizen-science project.

products.description: The open, community food database (ODbL) whose data powers tools like this one.

products.name: Mozilla Foundation

impact.note: State of Mozilla 2025 centers Mozilla's public-interest internet work on trustworthy AI, user agency and resisting tech concentration.

transparency.note: Mozilla Foundation publishes annual reports, Form 990s and audited financial statements.

ways_to_help.note: Support pathways include donating, participating in campaigns and using/recommending Mozilla resources.

openness.note: Mozilla supports open internet work and open-source projects, though the Foundation and Corporation structure is more complex than a pure volunteer commons.

longevity.note: Mozilla Foundation has published annual and financial reporting over many years and continues the open-internet mission.

products.description: Champions a healthy, open internet and user privacy, and stewards open-source projects like Firefox.

products.name: Internet Archive

impact.note: Internet Archive describes itself as a nonprofit digital library with free universal access to texts, media and archived web pages.

transparency.note: Internet Archive is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit and publishes IRS filings; Charity Navigator lists audited financial statements.

ways_to_help.note: People can donate money or materials and upload/preserve digital collections.

openness.note: The mission is open public access, though copyright litigation and controlled digital lending debates create real contested edges.

longevity.note: Internet Archive was founded in 1996 and has maintained major preservation infrastructure for decades.

products.description: A nonprofit digital library preserving the web, books, audio, and software for free public access.

products.name: Creative Commons

impact.note: Creative Commons' annual report frames CC licenses and tools as infrastructure for open sharing across culture, science and education.

transparency.note: Creative Commons publishes annual reports and public financial/governance documents.

ways_to_help.note: People can donate, use CC licenses, advocate for open access and participate in the CC community.

openness.note: Creative Commons licenses are explicitly designed to enable legal sharing and reuse.

longevity.note: Creative Commons marked 25 years of open-licensing infrastructure in its 2025 annual-report materials.

products.description: Builds and stewards the open licenses that let creators share work freely and legally.

products.name: OpenStreetMap Foundation

impact.note: OpenStreetMap is described as the largest open geographic database and infrastructure for many mapping projects.

transparency.note: The OpenStreetMap Foundation publishes official financial statements over many years.

ways_to_help.note: People can donate, become members, map, edit data and contribute to the OSM community.

openness.note: OpenStreetMap is open geodata infrastructure used and improved by a global contributor community.

longevity.note: The Foundation financials archive and long-running project infrastructure show a mature open-data commons.

products.description: Maintains open map infrastructure that powers humanitarian mapping, local knowledge, apps, and public-interest tools.

products.name: ProPublica

impact.note: ProPublica says its nonprofit investigative journalism exposes corruption and spurs real-world impact across the US.

transparency.note: ProPublica publishes annual reports, impact reports, Form 990s and financial statements.

ways_to_help.note: Support routes include donations, tips, local newsroom partnerships and sharing/using investigations.

openness.note: ProPublica publishes public-interest investigations and impact reports; it is not open-data infrastructure in the same sense as Wikimedia or OSM.

longevity.note: ProPublica launched in 2008 and has built a long record of nonprofit investigative reporting.

products.description: A nonprofit investigative newsroom whose reporting aims to expose corruption, abuse of power, and failures of public trust.

products.name: Partners In Health

impact.note: PIH's annual reports describe long-term health-equity work: care delivery, health-worker training and health-system strengthening.

transparency.note: PIH publishes annual reports, financial statements and Form 990s.

ways_to_help.note: Support is mainly through donations, advocacy and careers/volunteer-aligned participation.

openness.note: PIH publishes program and financial reporting, though its operating model is care delivery rather than open-data/open-source infrastructure.

longevity.note: PIH has worked on global health equity for decades and publishes a long archive of annual reports.

products.description: Builds long-term health systems and delivers care for the world's poorest communities.

products.name: The Trevor Project

impact.note: Trevor's annual reporting describes crisis services and suicide-prevention support for LGBTQ+ young people.

transparency.note: The Trevor Project publishes annual reports, IRS 990s and audited financial statements.

ways_to_help.note: Support routes include donations and trained volunteer crisis-counselor shifts.

openness.note: Trevor publishes financial and impact reporting, though crisis-care delivery is necessarily not open-data in the same way as knowledge commons.

longevity.note: Trevor has operated LGBTQ+ youth crisis and suicide-prevention services since 1998.

products.description: Provides 24/7 crisis support and suicide prevention for LGBTQ young people.

products.name: GiveWell

impact.note: GiveWell's mission is to find giving opportunities that save or improve lives the most per dollar.

transparency.note: GiveWell publishes its research reasoning, grantmaking process, feedback and organization-level transparency practices.

ways_to_help.note: Donors can give to specific top charities, funds or GiveWell operations depending on trust and risk preference.

openness.note: GiveWell maintains a public mistakes page so donors can evaluate its judgment and updates over time.

longevity.note: GiveWell has operated a public charity-research model since 2007 with a long archive of reviews and updates.

products.description: A research nonprofit that rigorously finds the highest-impact giving opportunities and routes donations to them.

products.name: Giving What We Can

impact.note: Giving What We Can helps donors find effective charities backed by research and routes attention toward high-impact giving opportunities.

transparency.note: Its public charity lists and cause-area pages explain why specific recommendations are considered strong giving opportunities.

ways_to_help.note: Supporters can donate through recommended charities and funds, take giving pledges, or use the site as a donor-learning hub.

openness.note: The site makes its recommendations and donor education materials publicly accessible, though some judgments depend on partner research.

longevity.note: The organization has been part of the public effective-giving ecosystem since 2009, giving it a longer record than many newer pledge groups.

products.description: A public effective-giving community that helps donors choose researched charities, pledge recurring giving, and compare high-impact cause areas.

products.name: Animal Charity Evaluators

impact.note: ACE recommends charities it judges most likely to create the greatest gains for animals and with demonstrated room for more funding.

transparency.note: ACE publishes its recommended charity list, evaluation materials and cause-prioritization resources for donors to review.

ways_to_help.note: Donors can give through the Recommended Charity Fund, support specific recommended charities, or use ACE's donor resources.

openness.note: ACE makes its broad evaluation framework and animal-advocacy resources public, though some grantmaking judgments remain expert-led.

longevity.note: ACE has an established public track record in animal charity evaluation and grantmaking rather than being a single campaign.

products.description: A specialist evaluator for farmed and wild-animal welfare giving, with recommended charities, grantmaking funds, and donor research.

products.name: Giving Green

impact.note: Giving Green evaluates climate nonprofits against scale, feasibility and funding need to guide high-impact climate donations.

transparency.note: Its research process describes how it identifies impact strategies, assesses organizations and publishes recommendations.

ways_to_help.note: Donors can use Giving Green's top climate nonprofit recommendations or contribute through its pooled fund model.

openness.note: Giving Green maintains an open research library that explains climate-giving strategies and recommendation updates.

longevity.note: Its climate-giving work has a shorter record than older watchdogs, so longevity is strong but not top-tier.

products.description: A climate-donation evaluator focused on high-impact nonprofits, policy change, and public research for donors.

products.name: Founders Pledge

impact.note: Founders Pledge researches pressing global problems and advises high-capacity donors on high-impact philanthropy.

transparency.note: Its public research database lets donors inspect cause investigations and recommended philanthropic strategies.

ways_to_help.note: Entrepreneurs and donors can pledge, use research, donate to programs and funds, or support the organization itself.

openness.note: A substantial body of research is public, but the advisory model is partly designed for member and donor relationships.

longevity.note: Founders Pledge operates registered nonprofit entities in several jurisdictions and has a multi-year record of philanthropic advising.

products.description: A pledge and advisory organization that turns startup-founder giving into researched global-health, climate, animal-welfare and longterm-risk philanthropy.

products.name: Charity Navigator

impact.note: Charity Navigator is best used as a donor due-diligence tool rather than a guarantee of highest impact per dollar.

transparency.note: Ratings draw on IRS data, partners and charity-provided information to help donors assess accountability and performance.

ways_to_help.note: Users can search rated nonprofits, compare causes and give through its Giving Basket.

openness.note: The site exposes charity profiles and ratings at large scale, making it useful for broad public checks before donating.

longevity.note: Charity Navigator reports more than 25 years of operation and a very large rated-charity database.

products.description: A mainstream charity-rating and donor-research site, useful for quick checks on accountability, finance, impact signals and giving logistics.

products.name: CharityWatch

impact.note: CharityWatch focuses on watchdog-style financial and accountability analysis, which supports donor due diligence more than direct impact measurement.

transparency.note: Its rating process examines fundraising efficiency, program spending and financial reporting rather than simply repeating charity claims.

ways_to_help.note: Donors can consult ratings, top-charity lists, giving tips and watchdog reports before deciding where to give.

openness.note: A meaningful portion of CharityWatch's donor guidance is public, while some deeper ratings content is membership-supported.

longevity.note: CharityWatch and its predecessor organization have operated for decades as a US charity watchdog.

products.description: A stricter US charity watchdog that emphasizes audited financial statements, fundraising efficiency and skepticism about inflated program claims.

products.name: BBB Wise Giving Alliance / Give.org

impact.note: Give.org is most valuable as a standards-based trust screen, not as a direct ranking of which charities do the most good.

transparency.note: BBB Wise Giving Alliance evaluates charities against 20 standards covering governance, finances, results reporting and transparency.

ways_to_help.note: Donors can look up national charity reports and use standards-based guidance before donating.

openness.note: Give.org makes charity reports and standards available publicly, making it useful as a free due-diligence stop.

longevity.note: The BBB charity-reporting lineage is one of the older donor-accountability systems in the US nonprofit sector.

products.description: A standards-based charity accountability resource for checking governance, finances, transparency, appeals and results reporting.

products.name: Candid / GuideStar

impact.note: GuideStar is most useful as nonprofit information infrastructure: it helps donors verify status and filings rather than ranking moral impact.

transparency.note: GuideStar helps users look up 501(c)(3) status, IRS Form 990s and nonprofit profile information.

ways_to_help.note: Donors, grantmakers and researchers can search nonprofit profiles, build lists and verify organizations before giving.

openness.note: A large public lookup layer is available, with deeper data and tools available through Candid products.

longevity.note: GuideStar/Candid has a long institutional role as US nonprofit data infrastructure.

products.description: Nonprofit data infrastructure for checking US charity status, IRS filings, profiles and grantmaking context before giving.

products.name: Center for High Impact Philanthropy

impact.note: The University of Pennsylvania center translates evidence into actionable giving guidance for donors and funders.

transparency.note: Its high-impact giving toolkits explain issue areas, giving opportunities and practical frameworks for philanthropic decisions.

ways_to_help.note: Donors can use toolkits, education programs and issue-area guidance to choose higher-impact gifts.

openness.note: The center publishes free public resources and toolkits, although it is not a charity-rating database.

longevity.note: As a university-based center, it has institutional continuity and an established archive of donor guidance.

products.description: A University of Pennsylvania research center that turns evidence into practical giving guidance, toolkits and education for donors.

products.name: GlobalGiving

impact.note: GlobalGiving gives donors access to vetted grassroots projects, making it useful for targeted support and disaster recovery giving.

transparency.note: Its vetting process reviews legitimacy, documents, capacity and compliance before organizations join the platform.

ways_to_help.note: Donors can support specific projects, send messages and receive updates from organizations they fund.

openness.note: Project pages and updates are public, though the platform is curated and not a fully open registry of all nonprofits.

longevity.note: GlobalGiving has vetted tens of thousands of social-change entities and has a long-standing platform role.

products.description: A global giving marketplace for vetted grassroots nonprofits and disaster-response projects, with project updates for donors.

products.name: GivingTuesday

impact.note: GivingTuesday mobilizes broad participation and local giving rather than selecting the most cost-effective charity for each donor.

transparency.note: Its public materials describe the decentralized movement, participation model and global generosity data work.

ways_to_help.note: Participants can give money, volunteer time, share voice, organize locally or use nonprofit/community toolkits.

openness.note: Any community or nonprofit can participate without needing centralized approval, which makes the movement highly accessible.

longevity.note: Created in 2012, GivingTuesday has become a year-round global movement with national movements in many countries.

products.description: A decentralized global generosity movement that helps people and nonprofits coordinate donations, volunteering, voice and local action.

products.name: One for the World

products.description: A long-running free-expression organization defending writers, journalists, readers and literary culture against censorship and intimidation.

products.name: OWASP Foundation

impact.note: OWASP works to improve software security through community-led open-source projects, chapters, education and conferences.

transparency.note: OWASP publishes a 2025 impact report and states that its community values include radical transparency from finances to code.

ways_to_help.note: Support routes include donation, membership, corporate support, local chapters, events, projects, online groups and Slack participation.

openness.note: OWASP says all projects, tools, documents, forums and chapters are free and open to anyone interested in application security.

longevity.note: OWASP says the foundation launched in 2001 and incorporated as a United States nonprofit charity in 2004.

products.description: A global open software-security commons behind widely used projects, standards, education and local chapters for safer web and application development.

products.name: Open Source Initiative

impact.note: OSI describes itself as a global nonprofit educating, advocating and building bridges across the open-source community.

transparency.note: OSI publishes its licensing role, board/team links, sponsor information, membership FAQ and policies around sponsor non-influence.

ways_to_help.note: People can support OSI through membership, one-time or recurring donations, sponsorship, discussions and community participation.

openness.note: OSI is the steward of the Open Source Definition and says it protects shared norms for what open source means.

longevity.note: OSI is a long-running 501(c)(3) nonprofit stewarding open-source licensing norms, with current programs including Open Source AI.

products.description: A standards-and-governance nonprofit for the open-source ecosystem, especially useful when you want to support the shared definition and licensing norms behind reusable software.

products.name: MuckRock Foundation

impact.note: MuckRock brings journalists, researchers and the public together to request, analyze and share government information.

transparency.note: MuckRock says its current financial statements are available on its financial transparency page and lists its 501(c)(3) status and EIN.

ways_to_help.note: Support routes include donations, newsletter subscription, using the request tools, trainings, crowdfunding public-records fees and community projects.

openness.note: MuckRock publishes public records, DocumentCloud tools, FOIA resources, data repositories, methodologies and open-records request archives.

longevity.note: MuckRock says it launched in 2010 and reincorporated as the nonprofit MuckRock Foundation in 2016.

products.description: A public-records and accountability nonprofit whose tools help people file FOIA requests, preserve documents, analyze records and publish investigative work.

products.name: Library Freedom Project

impact.note: LFP trains library workers and communities on privacy, intellectual freedom and information democracy.

transparency.note: The site explains LFP's network model, values, team, trainings, events and funders, but public financial detail is lighter than larger charities.

ways_to_help.note: Support and participation routes include regional hubs, talks, trainings, resources, events and the Library Freedom Institute community of practice.

openness.note: LFP publishes free presentations, posters, flyers and learning materials under a Creative Commons Attribution license.

longevity.note: The 2026 Library Freedom Institute page shows an ongoing 15-week training and continuing community of practice for library workers.

products.description: A library-worker network turning privacy, intellectual freedom and information democracy into trainings, resources and local advocacy inside public institutions.

products.name: The Engine Room

impact.note: The Engine Room says it has supported over 900 human-rights, climate and social-justice groups using data and technology across the Majority World.

transparency.note: The Engine Room publishes strategy, impact reporting, people pages, responsible data policy and a current Form 990 link.

ways_to_help.note: The strongest support routes are partnership, funding, newsletter engagement, jobs and use of its responsible-data resources rather than mass volunteering.

openness.note: The organization publishes research, strategy, impact materials and responsible-data guidance, but it is not primarily an open-source software commons.

longevity.note: The Engine Room's current strategy and 2025 impact report show an ongoing distributed nonprofit with a 2026-2028 plan.

products.description: A responsible-data and civil-society technology nonprofit supporting under-resourced and threatened social-justice groups with safer digital practice.

products.name: ARTICLE 19

impact.note: ARTICLE 19 works internationally on free expression, access to information, media independence, journalist protection and human rights in digital spaces.

ways_to_help.note: Support routes include donation, newsletter/community signup, research use, campaigns, partnerships and public advocacy.

openness.note: ARTICLE 19 publishes research and policy analysis on free expression, digital rights and internet freedom, including the Global Expression Report.

longevity.note: ARTICLE 19 says it has worked for more than 35 years and publishes annual reports and accounts back through prior years.

products.description: A global freedom-of-expression and information-rights organization with a substantial digital-rights, media-freedom and access-to-information research base.

products.name: Center for Internet Security

impact.note: CIS develops CIS Controls and Benchmarks and runs MS-ISAC support for U.S. state, local, tribal and territorial governments.

transparency.note: CIS publishes its mission, board/leadership links, year-in-review material, funding model and code/ethics material, though some offerings are paid.

ways_to_help.note: Support routes include membership, partnership, volunteer/community participation, careers, standards communities and use of CIS resources.

openness.note: CIS describes community-maintained Controls and over 100 vendor-neutral Benchmarks, while also funding work through paid tools and services.

longevity.note: CIS marks 25 years of creating confidence in the connected world and describes its origin in response to early internet security threats.

products.description: A nonprofit cybersecurity standards and services organization behind the CIS Controls, CIS Benchmarks and government cyber-threat sharing infrastructure.

products.name: Open Technology Fund

impact.note: OTF funds internet-freedom technologies, including privacy, security and anti-censorship tools for at-risk communities.

transparency.note: OTF publishes its values, fund programs, congressional remit and annual-report material, though grant decisions still require judgment.

ways_to_help.note: Support routes are mainly applying for funds, contributing to supported projects or following calls rather than mass-member volunteering.

openness.note: OTF's values emphasize open technology, user autonomy and community-led internet freedom work.

longevity.note: OTF describes a formal U.S. congressional remit and a record of funding internet-freedom projects over multiple years.

products.description: A funder for anti-censorship, privacy, circumvention and internet-freedom technologies used by journalists, civil society and at-risk communities.

products.name: noyb

impact.note: noyb brings strategic GDPR and privacy complaints against major technology and data companies across Europe.

transparency.note: noyb publishes annual reports covering activities, finances and governance.

ways_to_help.note: noyb offers membership and donation routes and explains its legal-work model publicly.

openness.note: noyb publishes many legal complaints, decisions and case materials, though legal strategy is not the same as open-source infrastructure.

longevity.note: noyb's annual-report archive shows multi-year operations as a dedicated European privacy-rights organization.

products.description: A European privacy-rights nonprofit using strategic legal complaints and public cases to enforce GDPR and data-protection rights.

products.name: European Digital Rights

impact.note: EDRi coordinates a European network advocating for privacy, free expression, platform accountability and rights-protecting technology policy.

transparency.note: EDRi publishes annual reports with governance, funding and program summaries.

ways_to_help.note: Support routes include donations, campaigns, member organizations, policy actions and public resources.

openness.note: EDRi publishes policy papers and public advocacy resources rather than operating primarily as a software project.

longevity.note: EDRi's report archive and long-running network role show established European digital-rights operations.

products.description: A European network for digital rights advocacy, policy research and civil-society coordination.

products.name: Bits of Freedom

impact.note: Bits of Freedom reports Dutch and European work on privacy, platform power, surveillance and digital rights campaigns.

transparency.note: Its 2024 annual report publishes program work, organization details and financial material.

ways_to_help.note: Support routes include donation, newsletter, campaigning and public participation around digital-rights issues.

openness.note: The organization publishes public campaign material and reports, though it is mainly an advocacy group rather than an open-data infrastructure project.

longevity.note: Bits of Freedom identifies as an established digital-rights organization and publishes annual reporting across campaigns and finances.

products.description: A Netherlands-based digital-rights organization working on privacy, surveillance, platform power and democratic technology policy.

products.name: Code for America

impact.note: Code for America reports civic-tech programs focused on benefits access, tax filing, criminal-record clearance and government service delivery.

transparency.note: The organization publishes impact reports, financial statements and Form 990 material.

ways_to_help.note: Support routes include donations, volunteer/civic-tech networks, careers, partnerships and public learning resources.

openness.note: Code for America shares public resources and some civic-tech methods, though government-service delivery can include closed partnerships and operational constraints.

longevity.note: Impact-report and financial archives show a mature U.S. civic-tech nonprofit with sustained operations.

products.description: A U.S. civic-technology nonprofit improving public-service delivery, benefits access and government digital capacity.

products.name: U.S. Digital Response

impact.note: U.S. Digital Response partners with governments and public servants on digital service delivery, grants, benefits and crisis-response capacity.

transparency.note: USDR publishes its mission, team model, resource library and yearly review, though it is younger than long-established civic institutions.

ways_to_help.note: USDR has a prominent volunteer model for technologists and operational experts supporting public agencies.

openness.note: USDR publishes resources and public case material, while much direct implementation work happens through agency partnerships.

longevity.note: USDR's 2024 year-in-review shows post-pandemic operations and capacity-building work, but its organizational history is shorter than legacy nonprofits.

products.description: A U.S. public-interest technology nonprofit that helps governments and public servants build practical digital capacity.

products.name: TechSoup

impact.note: TechSoup provides nonprofit technology access, validation, training and donated/discounted software through a global network.

transparency.note: TechSoup publishes year-in-review reporting on reach, programs and network activity.

ways_to_help.note: Support routes include donations, partnerships, local network participation, volunteering and nonprofit adoption of services.

openness.note: TechSoup emphasizes nonprofit access and capacity building, but much of its value comes through partner marketplaces and eligibility systems rather than open-source tools.

longevity.note: TechSoup describes a long-running global nonprofit technology network with broad cross-country reach.

products.description: A nonprofit technology-access network helping civil society organizations get software, training and digital capacity support.

products.name: Open Source Security Foundation

impact.note: OpenSSF coordinates open-source security initiatives, tools, standards and ecosystem programs, including Scorecard and supply-chain security work.

transparency.note: OpenSSF publishes annual reports, public resources, working-group material and security publications.

ways_to_help.note: OpenSSF offers working groups, projects, events, membership and adoption of its tools as participation routes.

openness.note: OpenSSF's Scorecard and related initiatives are public open-source ecosystem tools.

longevity.note: OpenSSF is an established Linux Foundation project area, though younger than some legacy public-interest institutions.

products.description: A foundation effort coordinating open-source security tools, standards, working groups and supply-chain resilience programs.

products.name: Digital Public Goods Alliance

impact.note: DPGA advances open-source digital public goods aligned with sustainable development, including a registry and ecosystem work.

transparency.note: DPGA publishes annual reports, roadmap material and public governance/resource pages.

ways_to_help.note: Participation routes include nominating digital public goods, community work, partner engagement and use of the DPG standard.

openness.note: The alliance centers open-source software, open data, open AI models, open standards and open content as digital public goods.

longevity.note: DPGA has a growing annual-report archive and roadmap, but it is newer than long-established technology nonprofits.

products.description: A global alliance promoting open-source digital public goods, standards and infrastructure for sustainable development.

products.name: Open Observatory of Network Interference

impact.note: OONI provides open tools, data and reports for measuring internet censorship and network interference around the world.

transparency.note: OONI publishes its methods, data, reports, software and organizational context publicly.

ways_to_help.note: Participation routes include running probes, using OONI Probe, analyzing data, translating, contributing code and supporting community measurements.

openness.note: OONI emphasizes free software, open data and public measurement methods for internet censorship research.

longevity.note: OONI describes more than a decade of censorship measurement work and global public datasets.

products.description: An open-data and open-source project that measures internet censorship and network interference worldwide.

products.name: Freedom House - Freedom on the Net

impact.note: Freedom on the Net provides country-level research and scoring on global internet freedom, censorship, surveillance and online rights.

transparency.note: Freedom House publishes its Freedom on the Net research methodology and country-scoring framework.

ways_to_help.note: Support is mainly through donations, advocacy use and research dissemination rather than hands-on volunteer pathways.

openness.note: The project publishes country reports, methodology and comparative research, though underlying research workflows are not fully open-data infrastructure.

longevity.note: Freedom on the Net has a long-running annual-report series and is embedded in Freedom House's broader research institution.

products.description: A global internet-freedom research program tracking censorship, surveillance, access barriers and online civil liberties.

products.name: Apache Software Foundation

impact.note: ASF stewards widely used open-source software projects and reports global infrastructure and community impact across many projects.

transparency.note: ASF publishes annual reports, board information, project statistics and foundation news.

ways_to_help.note: Participation routes include contributing to Apache projects, community governance, events, sponsorship and foundation support.

openness.note: ASF's core mission is open-source software under the Apache way, with public project governance and permissive licensing.

longevity.note: ASF has operated since 1999 and publishes long-running annual foundation reports.

products.description: A major open-source foundation stewarding Apache projects, community governance and public software infrastructure.

products.name: WaterAid

impact.note: WaterAid's annual reports describe clean-water, sanitation and hygiene reach and program approach across countries.

transparency.note: WaterAid publishes annual reports and says 80 cents of each donated dollar is reinvested in transforming lives with water, toilets and hygiene.

ways_to_help.note: Support routes include donations, fundraising and campaign engagement around water, sanitation and hygiene access.

openness.note: WaterAid shares annual impact and finance reports, but it is a program-delivery charity rather than an open-data commons project.

longevity.note: WaterAid has a long-running global WASH mission and a public archive of annual reports.

products.description: A global clean-water, sanitation and hygiene charity with clear annual reporting and direct donation routes.

products.name: UNICEF USA

ways_to_help.note: UNICEF USA provides donation, advocacy, education and fundraising routes for US supporters.

openness.note: UNICEF publishes a transparency portal and accountability material, though the work is large institutional aid rather than open-source infrastructure.

longevity.note: UNICEF is a long-running UN children's agency, and UNICEF USA maintains financial and annual-report archives for donors.

products.description: The US support arm for UNICEF's global child health, nutrition, education, protection and emergency-relief work.

products.name: Save the Children

impact.note: Save the Children's annual reporting covers child-focused work across conflict, displacement, disasters, poverty and resilience.

transparency.note: Save the Children publishes financial statements, charity ratings and donation-use information for donor review.

ways_to_help.note: Support routes include donations, child sponsorship, emergency funds, advocacy and campaigns.

openness.note: Save the Children publishes reports and accountability material, but the model is institutional program delivery rather than open public infrastructure.

longevity.note: Save the Children describes more than 100 years of work for children and maintains current annual reports.

products.description: A large child-focused humanitarian and development organization with long history, broad programs and multiple support paths.

products.name: Mercy Corps

transparency.note: Mercy Corps publishes annual reports, audited financial statements, Form 990s and institutional donor information.

ways_to_help.note: Support routes include donations, emergency response support, careers, partnership and advocacy around crisis resilience.

openness.note: Mercy Corps shares impact reports and financials, but its field-program model is not mainly open data or open-source infrastructure.

longevity.note: Mercy Corps maintains a long archive of annual reports and financial documents, with current 2025 reporting available.

products.description: A humanitarian organization working on crisis response, resilience, livelihoods and conflict-affected communities.

products.name: Oxfam

transparency.note: Oxfam publishes annual and financial reports, including archives and accountability materials.

ways_to_help.note: Support routes include donations, campaigns, advocacy and local Oxfam affiliate engagement.

openness.note: Oxfam publishes policy research and financial reports, but it is a large advocacy/program network rather than open public infrastructure.

longevity.note: Oxfam maintains a long-running international confederation and annual-report archive across affiliates.

products.description: A global confederation working on poverty, inequality, humanitarian response and advocacy, with substantial public reporting.

products.name: Human Rights Watch

impact.note: Human Rights Watch's World Report 2026 reviews human-rights practices and trends in more than 100 countries.

transparency.note: HRW publishes annual reports, Form 990s and financial statements, including 2025 documents.

ways_to_help.note: Support is mainly through donations, memberships, advocacy use and sharing investigations rather than mass volunteer delivery.

openness.note: HRW publishes reports, country research and financials openly, though underlying investigations are not an open-data project.

longevity.note: World Report 2026 is HRW's 36th annual review, showing a long-running human-rights reporting series.

products.description: A human-rights watchdog publishing country investigations, annual world reports and advocacy research.

products.name: Amnesty International

transparency.note: Amnesty publishes finance and pay information plus legal financial reports and accounts.

ways_to_help.note: Support routes include urgent actions, campaigns, donations, membership and country-section activism.

openness.note: Amnesty publishes annual human-rights reporting and public campaign materials, but not as open research infrastructure.

longevity.note: Amnesty maintains a long annual-report archive and global human-rights movement structure.

products.description: A global human-rights movement with public reports, campaigns, urgent actions and broad member/donor pathways.

ways_to_help.note: Support routes include donations, national chapter engagement, advocacy use and research dissemination.

openness.note: Transparency International publishes research, rankings, reports and anti-corruption resources for public use.

longevity.note: The organization maintains a multi-year annual-report archive and global chapter network focused on corruption accountability.
